Ana (Sales): Hey team — FinSight wants an EU-only POC. Main asks: 1) Guarantee inference traffic never leaves EU (including failover), 2) list of subprocessors + certifications, 3) any egress/pricing delta.
Priya (Solutions Eng): Quick Q — do they need hosted or would a Dedicated EU pool be acceptable? That changes ops work.
Mike (Presales): They prefer hosted for speed but said 'no US or non-EU processing ever' unless explicitly allowed. Concerned about capacity/failover.
Devon (EngOps): We support region pinning. Options: pin+reject (requests fail if no EU capacity) or pin+fallback (route to nearest region). Pin+reject preserves residency but hurts availability.
Sara (Legal): Also need: full subprocessor inventory for EU-hosted path, plus SOC2/ISO status per subprocessor, and confirmation that telemetry/monitoring is EU-hosted or redacted.
Priya (Solutions Eng): From memory: infra on GCP-eu (eu-west1, eu-central1), metrics via Datadog EU, logs to ELK EU cluster — but I'll validate.
Devon (EngOps): Paste of current policy snippet for clarity:
```
routing_policy:
  pin_region: [eu-west1, eu-central1]
  fallback: reject  # other option: fallback: global
  telemetry_redact: true
```
Ana (Sales): Customer also asked: if we choose pin+reject and we reserve dedicated EU capacity, what's the pricing delta vs standard hosted? Need a rough ballpark to include in deck.
Mike (Presales): Roughly — dedicated reserved lowers per-token variable by ~15-20% but adds a monthly commit (depends on GPU type). If we need standby headroom for peaks, that adds more fixed cost. I'll put numbers together.
Devon (EngOps): To guarantee no cross-border movement we must: 1) enforce routing_policy pin_region + fallback: reject, 2) provision KMS keys in EU (no key replication to non-EU), 3) ensure any third-party monitoring/storage is EU-localized and contractually restricted, 4) disable cross-region backups or ensure they stay in EU.
Sara (Legal): Also: what logs are retained for support/troubleshooting? If we redact PII but still ship stack traces to vendor A in US that's a no-go. Need dataflow diagram + retention windows.
Priya (Solutions Eng): I'll draft a 1-page options summary: Hosted-EU pin+reject (best residency, lowest availability), Hosted-EU pin+fallback (better availability, crosses boundary), Dedicated-EU (best SLA, higher fixed cost). Include required signoffs and lead times.
Ana (Sales): Timeline: customer wants POC start next week if we can commit. Priya can you draft by EOD? Mike can you add rough pricing ranges? Sara will list legal docs needed.
Mike (Presales): On it — pricing sketch by 12:00 PT.
Devon (EngOps): I'll validate subprocessors and certs and confirm telemetry endpoints. ETA = EOD.
Sara (Legal): I'll prepare checklist items for the security questionnaire: subprocessors table, dataflow diagram, KMS location, retention policy, incident response SLA.
Ana (Sales): Thanks all — looping in @security for visibility. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Note: there is no attached artifact. Please paste any diagrams or links here.
Priya (Solutions Eng): Will paste the one-pager + minimal dataflow link here once ready.
Ana (Sales): Customer also asked: if we do pin+reject, can we offer a manual DR override for emergencies with explicit customer consent? Pros/cons?
Devon (EngOps): Yes technically possible but requires contractual change and an ops playbook. Also need audit trail and customer-signed approval for each override. Not ideal for automated SLAs.
Sara (Legal): Manual DR override is acceptable only with written consent and explicit scope; require change to contract addendum.
Ana (Sales): Ok — include that as an optional add-on in the one-pager. Thanks team.
